title: Irish Whiskey
subtitle: From Dublin's four big distillers to two distilleries, and back
description: How Irish whiskey fell to two working distilleries by 1980, and how it grew again after 1987. Four pours.

pours.name: Redbreast 12 Year Old
pours.notes: Notice how it feels in your mouth before the flavour. People say unmalted barley makes it thick and oily.

pours.name: Bushmills 10 Year Old
pours.notes: Malted barley only, distilled three times. Put it beside the Redbreast and compare the weight.

pours.name: Powers Gold Label
pours.notes: Pot still whiskey blended with grain whiskey from a column still. Taste it after the Redbreast.

pours.name: Connemara Original Peated Single Malt
pours.notes: Peat smoke and two distillations, both unusual in Irish whiskey when Cooley started.
